description: Este grupo esta conformado por miembros del Club de Ciencia Tecnología y robótica RoboMinds.
summary: Project R.E.M.U.S (acronym for Radiation Exposure on Mars Using Simulations) is a finished prototype of a program/game that simulates what would the player do in cases of high or low doses of solar radiation.
details:
The REMUS project was made to be more complex at first, but then it was decided that we made a simpler Scratch version instead.

This very simple yet effective game lends you three decisions: If its okay to continue your experiments, if you have to take shelter, or if you have to get rest.

There is a bar that shows the energy, your remaining amount of oxygen, and the hypothetical martian base's shield durability. Clicking on the decision buttons leads to a certain change in the three bars, that lower or raise the percentage by 15.

The radiation is read in micrograys (μGy), and the variable of it is set to be randomly generated from 100 μGy to 1,000 μGy.

The cat character (affectionately referred to as Dal) of the game serves to act as a more useful visual indicator of the danger of the radiation present.

For information of the solar radiation of the martian environment, certain sources were used. Mainly, the information gathered was radiation level data from the MARIE (Mars Radiation Environment Experiment) instrument on board the 2001 Mars Odyssey spacecraft.

Everything you see in this game was manually made by a human, and no Super Intelligence (SI) was used.

Illustrations were done by Bianca Zaghi.

Backgrounds in-game were taken from the Perseverance Rover's photographs.
